sources.citation: Seiler, Walter. 1985. Imonda, a Papuan language (Pacific Linguistics B-93). Canberra: ANU. Appendix A 'Imonda and related languages', pp. 210-218 (Simog wordlist column p.212ff., Simog case-marker comparisons A.2-A.3).
sources.note: Nothing for Simog/Auwe: appendix gives comparative vocabulary and morphology (source/locative -m, noun classification) only; the book's stress statement (p.10, 'stress being approximately equal on all syllables') is about Imonda, not Simog.

sources.citation: Seiler, Walter. 1984. The main structures of Imonda: a Papuan language. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. hdl 1885/132956 (open access; PDF 23.4 MB + repository text). Simog material: ch.1 (classification, location east of Imonda), ch.6 pp.192-193 (Simog fik, faka, fea, faski vs Imonda classifier verbs), Appendix A (comparative wordlist Manem/Waris/Imonda/Daonda/Simog; number marking, nominaliser /i/, case markers -m/-ni/-ia, verb serialisation, with Simog sentence examples, c. pp.336-346).
sources.note: Nothing for Simog. The thesis's single prosodic remark, ch.2 'The sound system' p.20 - 'As far as suprasegmentals are concerned, tone and stress have no contrastive function, stress being approximately equal on all syllables' - is made of Imonda only (the chapter opens 'Imonda is a mainstream Trans-New Guinea (TNG) language as far as its consonant system is concerned'); Simog appears only in classification, morphosyntactic comparison and the appendix wordlist. Must not be transferred to Auwe.
